description: The transaction's `try`/`except`/`finally` is removed, which drops two separate behaviours. The connection is no longer closed on the error path, so any insert that raises leaks a pooled connection; and a `ConstraintViolation` is no longer rolled back and returned as 0, so callers that relied on that contract now see the exception escape mid-transaction. Both are labeled: one correct finding about the second defect would otherwise score as a false positive and raise this case's false-positive floor permanently. The happy path is unchanged, which is what makes either easy to miss.

expected.title: Constraint violation no longer rolls back the transaction
